- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
  Location: security_pass_sync_final_pr_if_unmergeable(), last command (around line 11721 in the new file, just before the closing `}`)
  Issue: The function relies on bash's natural exit-status propagation — its return value is whatever `sync_default_into_integration_branch` last returned, because no other command follows it. The new test (`test_sync_failure_is_returned_so_the_tick_stops_for_the_project`) does pin the current behavior, but a future edit that adds any command after the sync call (logging, an additional check, a trailing `return 0`) silently breaks the `if ! security_pass_sync_final_pr_if_unmergeable ...` gate at the call site (the `continue` branch becomes unreachable, so a sync failure no longer skips the project for this tick).
  Suggested minimal fix: Replace the trailing `sync_default_into_integration_branch "${integration_branch}" "${default_branch}"` with `sync_default_into_integration_branch "${integration_branch}" "${default_branch}" || return $?` (or `... || return 1`) to make the propagation explicit and survive future edits. Existing test still passes; no other call site changes.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
